title: PLEASE STOP RELEASING UNTESTED UPDATES
creator: rousea
content:
I use a number of add-ons that greatly enhance Thunderbird but they keep breaking as new updates are released:

Cardbook is a very useful address book add-on, integrating with my Google address book. However a few months ago it stopped working when a Thunderbird update was automatically installed (I think it was V158). The only way of overcoming this was to revert back to the ESR (Extended Support Release). That wasn't compatible with the database that had been modified by the latest release. Fortunately I had a back-up copy of the previous database which I had to recover.

A couple of months ago a new release stopped Cardbook working. By trial and error I discovered that Cardbook had been updated for compatibility with the latest Thunderbird release so I was able to restore normal operation by updating to Thunderbird V158.

Now Thunderbird has updated to V159 and Cardbook has stopped working again. If I open Cardbook it shows the address book completely empty. The Add-on Manager doesn't flag any compatibility issues. This is disasterous for me as I am totally dependent on using Cardbook.

Lightning Calendar Tabs is another useful add-on, giving access to my Google Calendar through a icon in the task bar. However that has also stopped working under V159. The Add-on Manager shows it as being incompatible with V159.

So why does Mozilla keep releasing updates that stop add-ons from working?. Can I revert back to V158 and stop further updates?

title: Handling stale folders
creator: firefox2975
content:
Hi,

I've started experimenting with Vibecoding some extensions for myself.. But I keep hitting a problem where TB reports back that folders are stale.

Specifically I'll hit something like this:

[Exception... "Component returned failure code: 0x80550005 (NS_MSG_ERROR_FOLDER_SUMMARY_OUT_OF_DATE) [nsIMsgFolder.messages]" nsresult: "0x80550005 (NS_MSG_ERROR_FOLDER_SUMMARY_OUT_OF_DATE)" location: "JS frame :: resource:///modules/ExtensionMessages.sys.mjs :: getMessagesInFolder :: line 925" data: no] ExtensionMessages.sys.mjs:928:13 [Exception... "Component returned failure code: 0x80550005

Usually when I go look at these folders in the UI, the total-email-count for the folder in blank, but the Size of the folder will show >1kb (eg .. something greater than zero). If I click on the folder, TB updates the summary file and all is well, for a while.

Some folders do report as no messages, and "blank" for file size as well.. but those seem to be genuinely empty.

These types of issues are causing pain in several extension ideas I've had, and I can't seem to figure out a way to handle them.

For example: I had an idea to create and extension to delete empty folders. The original version would encounter these NS_MSG_ERROR_FOLDER_SUMMARY_OUT_OF_DATE folders, and then just wipe them out as TB told the extension there were no emails in it. I found this out a little too late for some folders..

Another idea was to create and manage Virtual Search folders automatically. But I've hit a similar issue there with this staleness and had to skip such folders.

I've tried to get the extensions to trigger rebuilding summary files when we hit this error, but that never seems to do the job. The only method I've found is to open the folder manually in TB. Sometimes I'll find that starting a Search across the folders also helps - but that also tends to bail out unexplained.

I'm working with a lot of emails and folders..

If anyone can help explain why TB "forgets" whats in a folder, and how to trigger a summary-rebuild for a specific folder I'd be interested in hearing it.

Thanks

title: How to get past Confirm Security Exception
creator: jjc2
content:
Thunderbird has worked fine for me over the years. I rarely send mail but started receiving a message that smpt server refused connection and contacted Network Solutions support. Their advice is below but I have clicked Clear Security Exception many times but can't get beyond it. Any ideas would be welcome.

To configure your mailbox in Thunderbird, please follow these steps: 

   Open the Thunderbird application.    Select Add Mail Account.    Enter your Full Name, Email Address, and Password.    Click Continue.     When you reach the page titled "Connect your email settings", click Edit Configuration.    Change both the Incoming Server Hostname and Outgoing Server Hostname to mymail2.myregisteredsite.com.    Click Connect.    Enter your mailbox password when prompted.    After entering the password, a warning message may appear. Select Confirm Security Exception.

Please note that you may need to click Confirm Security Exception three or four times before the account setup is completed successfully.

The reason you are receiving the security warning is that the mailbox is configured to use Connection Security: None. This is necessary because your mailbox is hosted on a legacy email service that is not compatible with SSL/TLS or STARTTLS encrypted connection methods. As a result, Thunderbird may display security warnings during the configuration process.

If you require further assistance with Thunderbird configuration, we recommend contacting your personal IT professional or someone familiar with email client setup and administration, as third-party email client configuration falls outside our support scope.
